title: Launcher
responsibility: Install and run the shell from one documented command: build the application and start it in production mode, owning the `next start` process as a child, forwarding shutdown to it, waiting for it to exit, and leaving nothing behind — no process on the port, no temporary directory it created. The file watcher is an in-process resource of the child and is released by its teardown.
notes: ⚠️ PLANNED, NOT BUILT (2026-08-27). `implementedBy` is absent, and its absence is the only signal in this artifact that says so — the same convention CMP-0011 established, and the same hazard QST-0015 named: creating these records takes the orphan count to zero while nothing exists. 'Every requirement traces to a component' becomes true; 'the shell works' does not. ⚠️ PRODUCTION MODE ONLY (DEC-0018): `next build` then `next start`. `next dev` is a contributor workflow and is not a shipped configuration — AST-0015 showed the two produce different artifacts, so shipping the development server would mean shipping something this project can never validate. ⚠️ THE PROCESS OWNERSHIP IS AN OBLIGATION WITH NO MECHANISM YET, deliberately. The skeleton creates its watcher on `listen` and closes it in its own `close()`, but that belongs to a process owning its own HTTP server; under `next start` there is no such object and nothing has been run. Choosing and validating the binding is this component's design work. ⚠️ PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-27 BY TSK-0003, and `implementedBy` now points at the scaffold. Read it as exactly what QST-0015's answer says it means — CODE EXISTS — and nothing more. What exists is the Next.js application, a production build, a loopback start script and one route that responds. What does NOT exist is the thing this component is mostly about: a launcher that owns both the application process and the file watcher and terminates the watcher with it. There is no watcher yet to own. ⚠️ BOTH ITS CRITERIA REMAIN `not-evaluated`, deliberately. ACC-0033 (installs and starts from one documented command) is not satisfied by two scripts a reader has to compose themselves, and ACC-0032 (stopping the launcher leaves nothing behind) has nothing to stop. TSK-0013 finishes both. This is the state the planned/built axis was rejected for being unable to express: a populated `implementedBy` beside unevaluated criteria says 'some code, unjudged' precisely, where a boolean would have had to lie in one direction or the other. ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-08-29: THERE IS NO SECOND PROCESS, AND THERE NEVER WAS ONE TO OWN. This artifact previously said the launcher owns 'both the application process and the file watcher' and 'terminates the watcher with the application'. The watcher is chokidar, imported dynamically INSIDE the `next start` process and held by the change-stream service in that process's memory. A parent launcher cannot call `changeStream.close()` across that boundary without adding IPC or a shutdown endpoint, and neither is justified for a local-first tool. The old wording described a mechanism that could not be built, which is worse than an unmet obligation: it would have been 'satisfied' by a launcher that called nothing and reported success. ⚠️ WHAT IS TRUE INSTEAD, and all of it is enforceable. The launcher owns ONE child: the `next start` process. The change-stream service owns its watcher and closes it when its last subscriber leaves — already built and tested under TSK-0011. Terminating the application process releases any watcher still open through process teardown, which is the operating system's guarantee rather than the launcher's. `close()` stays what it is: a service and test lifecycle operation, never something the launcher claims to call across a process boundary. ⚠️ THIS COMPONENT'S DESIGN WORK SHRANK RATHER THAN GREW. Its notes called 'choosing and validating the binding' the substance of the component; there is no binding to choose. What is left is a real and checkable job: one command, an absolute content root printed at startup, loopback bound explicitly, shutdown forwarded, the child waited for, and a bounded escalation if it does not go. ⚠️ BUILT 2026-08-29 BY TSK-0013 (EVD-0073). ACC-0032 and ACC-0033 pass. ⚠️ IT OWNS ONE CHILD AND SAYS SO. `next start` is spawned directly with Node, so the pid it holds IS the server's — through `npm run` it would hold a shim, and on Windows a `.cmd` shim whose child does not reliably receive a forwarded signal. ⚠️ THE CONTENT ROOT IS ABSOLUTE AND PRINTED, and a missing one is exit code 2 rather than a fallback. The application would otherwise resolve to its own directory and be correct with no way for the operator to know WHICH directory — #70's refusal-to-guess at the launcher. ⚠️ ITS RUN DIRECTORY EXISTS PARTLY SO CLEANUP CAN BE OBSERVED. It carries the run record a supervisor reads to find the child; its removal is one of ACC-0032's three observations, and a launcher with no temporary state would make that clause vacuous. ⚠️ ACC-0033 RE-EVALUATED 2026-08-29 (EVD-0074) after being marked `pass` on evidence that disclaimed the install branch. It now rests on a cold run: no `node_modules`, no `.next`, install branch taken and asserted, content root verified to be inside the copy rather than the source repository.
